title: Parking lot design
idea: A parking lot design turns "park, pay, leave" into a few classes: spots that know their size, tickets that record entry, and a swappable pricing rule.

analogy.text: A cloakroom. The attendant finds a free hook that fits your coat, hands you a numbered tag, and charges by the hour when you return.
analogy.breaks: A real lot has many gates working at the same moment.

points: Nouns in the requirements become classes: `Spot`, `Ticket`, `ParkingLot`, `HourlyPricing`.
Each `Spot` decides whether a vehicle fits, so size rules live in one place.
`ParkingLot` owns the search and the ticket map; callers never touch spots directly.
Pricing is an injected strategy, so a new fee rule is a new class.

hero.title: One car in, one car out

messages.label: park(vehicle, now)
messages.note: The driver arrives. `ParkingLot` runs the search; the driver never picks a spot.

messages.label: fits(vehicle)?
messages.note: The lot asks each `Spot` in order. A spot says yes only if it is free and large enough.

messages.label: yes
messages.note: The first spot that fits wins. A smarter selection rule could be another strategy.

messages.label: Ticket
messages.note: The lot marks the spot taken and returns a `Ticket` with vehicle, spot and entry time.

messages.label: leave(plate, now)
messages.note: At exit the lot finds the ticket by plate. An unknown plate is an error, not a free exit.

messages.label: price(ticket, now)
messages.note: The fee rule lives outside the lot. Swap in weekend or flat pricing without editing `ParkingLot`.

messages.label: fee, spot freed
messages.note: The spot becomes free again and the ticket is removed, so the next car can use it.

code.title: Spots, tickets, pricing
code.caption: Times are minutes passed in by the caller, so the run is repeatable. Add a `FlatPricing` class and pass it in.

walk.text: Sizes are ranked numbers. A smaller vehicle may use a larger spot, never the reverse.
The pricing strategy rounds up to whole hours and charges by vehicle type.
Spots and pricing are injected: the lot depends on their shape, not their class.
`park` refuses a plate already parked, then claims the first fitting spot and records the ticket.
`leave` checks the ticket, frees the spot, then delegates the fee.
The second car fills the truck spot, so the truck is refused. Once KA-1 leaves, A2 takes KA-4.

pitfalls: Do not read the system clock inside `park`; pass time in so tests stay repeatable.
Keep fee rules out of `ParkingLot`, or every new tariff edits a working class.
Two gates can grab one spot at once; claim spots atomically in a multi-gate system.

quiz.why: `Math.max(1, …)` charges at least one hour. 61 minutes rounds up to two hours; 120 is exactly two.

takeaway: Spots judge fit, tickets record entry, and pricing is a swappable strategy.

starters: How would I add multiple floors and an entry display board?
How do two entry gates avoid giving out the same spot?
Which design patterns do interviewers expect in a parking lot?
